another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment Result

I've completed the assessment for **Alex**, and unfortunately, based on the current circumstances, you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit.

### Summary for Alex (age 11):

**Result: INELIGIBLE** ❌

### Here's why:

You meet many of the fundamental requirements:
- ✅ Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
- ✅ You live in the UK and meet residency requirements
- ✅ You contribute £50/week towards Alex's upkeep, which demonstrates financial responsibility
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✅ Alex is not working full-time, receiving benefits, or in a disqualifying apprenticeship

**However, the issue is:**
- ❌ Alex has been in hospital or residential accommodation for **15 weeks**, which exceeds the **12-week maximum** allowed period

### Important Exception:

Child Benefit can continue beyond 12 weeks in hospital **if you are regularly spending money on Alex** during their hospital stay. This could include:
- Buying clothes or personal items for them
- Providing pocket money
- Paying for visits to see them
- Purchasing treats or gifts
- Any other ongoing expenses for their benefit

### What You Should Do:

**If you ARE regularly spending money on Alex while they're in hospital:**
- You should contact HMRC directly to explain your situation
- Provide evidence of your ongoing spending
- You may still qualify under the exception to the 12-week rule

**Contact HMRC Child Benefit:**
- Phone: 0300 200 3100
- Online: [www.gov.uk/child-benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit-for-children-in-hospital-or-care)

They can review your specific circumstances and determine if the exception applies to your case.

Do you have any questions about this assessment?

tool_response.question: Has the child's cumulative time in hospital or residential accommodation exceeded 12 weeks?
tool_response.help_text: Child Benefit continues for up to 12 weeks in hospital/residential accommodation. CUMULATIVE RULE: If child returns within 28 days of leaving, time counts towards 12-week limit. Multiple stays within 28 days are added together.

criteria.calculation_method: Sum all hospital/residential stays. If gap between stays is less than 28 days, count both stays towards cumulative total. If gap is 28+ days, reset counter.
criteria.example: 10 weeks hospital + 15 day gap + 3 weeks hospital = 13 weeks cumulative (exceeds limit)

tool_response.help_text: Exception to 12-week rule if you regularly spend money on child. For hospital abroad, only if they went abroad for treatment and you're back in UK. Partner's spending counts if married/civil partnered and living together.
